Composed workflows / outcome systems

Playbooks compose the system.

A playbook coordinates personas, skills, workflows, evidence, artifacts, and quality gates around a meaningful outcome. It is the layer for work that is larger than any one persona or skill.

How the layers fit

The library stays understandable when each layer has one job. Personas describe who is operating, Skills describe what they can do, Operating Packs provide domain or project context, Tool-use recipes make a capability practical in a named tool, and Playbooks coordinate the work.

A Playbook is a reusable operating model for an outcome.

It defines stages, participants, handoffs, decision rights, shared state, quality gates, and learning loops. It references Personas, Skills, Operating Packs, and Tool-use recipes without copying their definitions.

01 / Primitives

Personas + Skills

The reusable people and expertise behind the work.

  • Personas and operating conditions
  • Portable Skills and quality signals
  • Relevant evidence and resources
02 / Context

Operating Packs

Persistent domain or project rules that govern how the work is performed.

  • Standards, conventions, and procedures
  • References and validation guidance
  • Source, entrypoint, and availability
03 / Translation

Tool-use recipes

The task-specific binding that makes a Skill usable in a particular Tool.

  • Required capability and prerequisites
  • Bounded steps and permissions
  • Output, fallback, and verification
04 / Composition

Workflows + stages

The way work is organized and handed off toward an outcome.

  • Foundational, supporting, and edge flows
  • Activities, artifacts, and owners
  • Decision points and quality gates

Operating Pack and Template references

A Playbook may require persistent domain context at one or more stages and may start from a known reusable artifact. Reference each by stable identity and scope instead of copying its rules or structure into the outcome model.

Design System context + starting structure

The Design System Operating Pack supplies contextual conventions and validation guidance. A Playbook can reference a Template such as Web App Design System when the outcome starts from a known reusable artifact. The Template owns starting structure; the Playbook still owns participants, stages, handoffs, approvals, gates, shared state, and outcome.

Bounded parallel implementation

Coordinate a small number of independent repository workstreams without paying for stale assumptions, duplicated inspection, nested agents, polling, or child-transcript synthesis. Orient the implementer and source-ground in the target repository before dispatch. This is a system Playbook, not a rewrite of Multi-Persona Collaboration.

Bounded parallel implementation

A thin coordinator records each implementer's orientation state, verifies the target repository's orientation path, and source-grounds each candidate before dispatching one implementer per confirmed or qualified workstream. Each implementer owns one repository slice, one branch, and one PR, then stops. The coordinator returns one compact handoff or supported completion callback. Review reinspects current GitHub state and current owner/source. Merge stays a separate authorized mutation.

Working model
01 / ORIENTCheck implementer contextRecord fresh, previously oriented, or unknown. Follow the target repository's orientation path before grounding.
02 / GROUNDSource-ground current truthInspect current target-repository instructions, source, and tests. Classify confirmed, qualified, or contradicted.
03 / DISPATCHBound confirmed workstreamsSend only confirmed or qualified packets with orientation references/status. One level of delegation only.
04 / IMPLEMENTOne workstream eachRe-open current source, stay in scope, open one PR or stop blocked, then stop.
05 / HANDOFFReturn references or callbackCollect compact status for review_ready, blocked, or deferred. No child transcripts.
06 / REVIEWReinspect GitHubJudge the live PR and whether it still matches current owner and source. The handoff or callback is not current truth.
07 / CORRECTFix named defectsSend only scoped correction back to the same workstream. Still no merge.
08 / MERGEAuthorize separatelyRefresh state and merge only with explicit authorization, then stop.
CoordinatorVerify orientation, source-ground, dispatch confirmed or qualified packets, collect compact handoffs, and stop. Do not reimplement or review during this stage.
ImplementerOrient to the target repository, then own one workstream, one repository, one branch, one PR, required validation, then stop.
ReviewerIndependent GitHub reinspection and problem-correctness against current owner/source. Separate blockers from suggestions.
AuthorizerMerge and other consequential mutations after fresh preflight.

Orientation preflight

Fresh, previously oriented, or unknown, with the target repository's entrypoint and completion evidence.

Source-grounding result

Confirmed, qualified, or contradicted against current target-repository source. Contradicted work is not dispatched.

Branch and pull request

GitHub is the source of current implementation, diff, review, and check state.

Compact handoff or callback

Reference-based status for review_ready, blocked, or deferred. Notification only.

Runtime adapters

Supported callbacks return to the originating conversation; unsupported runtimes use the same coordinator fallback. The Playbook stays runtime-neutral.

Shared state keeps the playbook coherent

The Playbook keeps work coherent through shared objects. Riley coordinates contributors against that state; specialists own domain judgment and disposition. Each stage should read from and leave behind a traceable record.

Source-grounded context brief

Reader, goal, target, constraints, original source versions, proposed positioning, and unresolved questions. Use the application brief.

Evidence bank

Source experiences, outcomes, artifacts, decisions, metrics, confidence, and gaps.

Job opportunity ledger

Durable private search state for discovered roles, deduplication, disposition, and resurfacing rules. Owned by the search specialist capability, not Riley. Ledger contract.

Artifact versions and reviews

Each review names a version, criterion, passage/page, finding, action, and verdict. Reopen affected checks after edits. Review contract.

Decision + learning log

What changed, why it changed, what remains uncertain, and what would change the plan again.

What belongs in a playbook skill?

Yes, eventually. A dedicated playbooks skill should define outcomes, decompose stages, route work to existing personas and skills, manage shared state, enforce quality gates, preserve decision rights, and close the learning loop. It should call persona-research and persona-skills when new lenses or capabilities are needed instead of recreating their methods.

Change control

A playbook is not complete when one stage finishes; it is complete when the shared state and downstream artifacts are coherent.

Every playbook update ends with a conditional reconciliation gate.

When a stage changes a source, record, artifact, handoff, or quality gate, invoke $change-impact-reconciliation before handing the playbook back. Re-check participants, prerequisites, shared state, dependent artifacts, and the next stage. Read-only consultation stages skip the gate; prototype stages check isolation only.

Coordinate research, creation or adaptation, promotion when justified, maintenance, and reconciliation for reusable Templates. Elena Park stewards the collection; domain specialists own substantive quality; Mara escalates architecture. Canonical starters stay in the verified external source.

Research, promote, and maintain a reusable Template

Use this Playbook when the Template outcome crosses stewardship and another owner. For a bounded Skill action alone, stay on the Templates routes instead.

Working model
01 / DEFINEScope the needCapture destination, authorization, and whether broader reuse is claimed.
02 / DISCOVERSearch and verifyCatalog-first discovery with truthful source path, entrypoint, and revision evidence.
03 / ROUTEHand off domain qualitySend substantive work to the smallest capable specialist; escalate architecture to Mara.
04 / COMPOSECreate or adaptBuild only the smallest useful starter after the boundary is accepted.
05 / VALIDATEProve the boundaryCheck source truth, starter boundary, and required specialist quality.
06 / LIFECYCLEKeep local or promotePromote only with reuse evidence and authorization; otherwise keep the starter local.
07 / RECONCILEReview onceRun Template reconciliation, then one universal change-impact pass when required.
